FLASHCARD SET · AGES 6–9 MONTHS

Animals & Everyday Objects Flashcards

Twelve cards for the Baby 1 stage: six animals ready for sounds and six everyday things ready for pointing — your baby’s widening world, one card at a time.

These cards belong to Baby 1 on the Kiddo School learning path.

THE CARDS

Every card in the set.

Each card has its own page: the picture and short, practical notes for grown-ups — what it is for, how to use it, how to print it. Tap any card to open it.

HOW TO USE THESE CARDS

Four ways that work.

You do not need a plan or a printer schedule. Pick one idea, try it for two minutes and see what happens.

  1. 01

    Animals make noise

    For every animal card, add its sound. At this age the sound is the hook — your baby may laugh, copy or stare; all three are learning.

  2. 02

    Point, then wait

    Tap the picture, say the word, then stay quiet. Pointing back at a card is a big 6–9-month milestone — give it room to happen.

  3. 03

    Real-world replays

    Each card has a real twin somewhere: the dog on your street, the spoon in the drawer. Meeting the word twice is the lesson.

  4. 04

    Follow the stare

    Whatever card your baby studies longest, do that one again tomorrow. Interest is the engine of the whole stage.

      Cat Flashcard for Babies

      A soft, watchy cat. Cats are a favourite first animal — small enough to feel safe, full of personality, and famous for a sound every baby can try.

      What this card names

      Gives your baby one clear cat face to study while the word cat lands softly.

      Point and say

      Say cat while tapping the soft ears, then wait for a sound back.

      What it builds

      Builds first-word listening plus the slow back-and-forth of early talk.

      Print tips

      Cardstock with rounded corners keeps lap-sized hands safe.

      Baby tip

      A soft voice keeps the moment calm and the looking long.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Cat lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Animals & Everyday Objects for Babies 6–9 Months class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · ANIMALS & EVERYDAY OBJECTS · AGES 6–9 MONTHS

      Dog Flashcard for Babies

      A happy, tongue-out dog. Dogs bring their own sound and action — barking and tail-wagging are easy to act out, which makes this card a full mini-performance.

      What this card names

      The printed dog gives your baby a friendly face to match a word you already say.

      Point and say

      Tap the tail, say dog, and let the quiet afterwards do its work.

      What it builds

      Feeds sound recognition and early imitation, the seed of every copied word.

      Print tips

      Thick paper holds up best against the dribble and gumming it meets.

      Baby tip

      Any dog you meet on the pram route counts as a replay.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Dog lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Animals & Everyday Objects for Babies 6–9 Months class on the Learning Path.

      Bird Flashcard for Babies

      A bright little bird. Birds move fast and catch the eye — naming them turns window-watching into a real language moment.

      What this card names

      Fixes a still bird in view, so fast wings become something your baby can name.

      Point and say

      Point and say bird, then watch the window for a real one.

      What it builds

      Sharpens distance tracking and links one word to a moving thing.

      Print tips

      A strong, dark print keeps the little bird clear from pram distance.

      Baby tip

      Stop after one or two cards; short is right at this age.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Bird lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Animals & Everyday Objects for Babies 6–9 Months class on the Learning Path.

      Fish Flashcard for Babies

      A round, friendly fish. Fish are calm and quiet — a nice change of pace in an animal set, and their gulping mouths are fun to imitate.

      What this card names

      Offers a calm, quiet picture between the louder animal cards in the stack.

      Point and say

      Trace the round mouth with one slow finger as you say fish.

      What it builds

      Grows quiet attention and close study of faces, mouths and gentle sounds.

      Print tips

      Plain white paper is fine, but matte cardstock kills window glare.

      Baby tip

      Slow everything down; a calm card works best with a calm voice.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Fish lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Animals & Everyday Objects for Babies 6–9 Months class on the Learning Path.

      Duck Flashcard for Babies

      A cheerful duck. With its sound, its waddle and its pond life, the duck is practically a ready-made baby game.

      What this card names

      Turns a cheerful picture into a word your baby will grin at all week.

      Point and say

      Point at the duck, say the word, then find one on the pram route.

      What it builds

      Wires sound to laughter, so the word arrives inside a happy moment.

      Print tips

      Laminate this one if bath-side showing is part of the plan.

      Baby tip

      If the giggles come, stay with this card a moment longer.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Duck lesson on the Learning Path.

      Cow Flashcard for Babies

      A big, gentle cow. Cow is a sound-and-size animal: huge, slow and famous for one long, easy-to-copy note.

      What this card names

      Puts a big, gentle animal in view, with the longest sound in the set.

      Point and say

      Offer one long moo after you say cow, then stop and smile.

      What it builds

      Trains the ear to follow one long sound from start to finish.

      Print tips

      Print it big — a page-wide cow reads easily from your lap.

      Baby tip

      Try the moo once, quietly, and see what your baby does.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Cow lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Animals & Everyday Objects for Babies 6–9 Months class on the Learning Path.

      Ball Flashcard for Babies

      A bright, bouncy ball. The everyday half of the set begins: a thing your baby has probably already pushed, dropped and chased.

      What this card names

      Names the first toy most babies chase, in a shape their eyes love.

      Point and say

      Roll a soft ball towards your baby and say ball as it moves.

      What it builds

      Strengthens eye tracking of moving things and the reach that follows them.

      Print tips

      Cardstock plus rounded corners survives the reaching and batting it invites.

      Baby tip

      Let reaching hands touch the card — an adult holds it always.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Ball lesson on the Learning Path.

      Shoe Flashcard for Babies

      A simple shoe. Shoes mark every outing, so this word comes with a built-in routine: shoes on, shoes off, all day long.

      What this card names

      Labels a thing your baby sees at every doorway and changing mat.

      Point and say

      Tap the picture, then say shoe when the real ones go on at the door.

      What it builds

      Anchors a routine word your baby will hear many times every day.

      Print tips

      Two copies work well — changing bag and hallway.

      Baby tip

      Say the word in real routines rather than drilling at the card.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Shoe lesson on the Learning Path.

      Cup Flashcard for Babies

      An everyday cup, back from the earlier sets — familiarity is the point. Your baby now meets the same word in a new set, which is exactly how memory works.

      What this card names

      Shows the everyday object your baby reaches for at every meal.

      Point and say

      Hold the card by the highchair and say cup when the drink arrives.

      What it builds

      Connects the word to an object your baby grips, taps and drinks from.

      Print tips

      Keep a spare copy in the kitchen, where most cup moments happen.

      Baby tip

      Follow your baby's interest; a glance at the real cup counts fully.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Cup lesson on the Learning Path.

      Spoon Flashcard for Babies

      A shiny spoon. Meals give this word a stage several times a day — no other card in the set gets so many live performances.

      What this card names

      Brings the shiniest thing on the tray into your baby's word range.

      Point and say

      Say spoon as the shiny one lands on the tray, then let your baby reach.

      What it builds

      Links a mealtime tool to its name through daily, familiar repetition.

      Print tips

      A bright, clean print matters less than showing it often at meals.

      Baby tip

      Keep meal naming light — one clear word beats a running commentary.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Spoon lesson on the Learning Path.

      Car Flashcard for Babies

      A speedy little car. Cars whoosh past windows and parking lots all day — one of the most-repeated baby words in the world, and this card gives it a face.

      What this card names

      Captures the moving thing your baby watches most from windows and prams.

      Point and say

      Point at the car and say the word when a real one passes the window.

      What it builds

      Builds tracking of faraway moving things, the window words of babyhood.

      Print tips

      Sturdy card suits this one, since the pram pocket is its home.

      Baby tip

      Watch for the stare at passing cars; that is the word landing.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Car lesson on the Learning Path.

      Teddy bear Flashcard for Babies

      A soft teddy bear closing the set. For many babies this word names an actual best friend — the strongest possible ending for the Baby 1 stage.

      What this card names

      Holds a picture of the friend your baby already hugs at bedtime.

      Point and say

      Hold the card next to the real bear at bedtime and say its name.

      What it builds

      Nurtures comfort and naming together, the warmest kind of first word.

      Print tips

      Cardstock with a wipe-clean sleeve — bedtime cards meet drool.

      Baby tip

      End card time here if your baby is sleepy and content.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Teddy bear lesson on the Learning Path.
